- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates in the middle to late period when prices are trending upward or recovering — often overshooting the true value by 2–5%.
- Shows significant lag in responding to recent price spikes; forecasts lag behind actual price movements by 5–10 days.
- Tends to overcorrect after sharp declines, leading to premature recovery signals that are too aggressive.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring structural or seasonal trends.
- Underestimates volatility in the final 5–7 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true outcomes show sudden upward or downward corrections.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model often fails to capture the momentum, underestimating the continuation or acceleration.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model often overestimates the continuation, failing to recognize potential reversal or support levels.
